issues.claim: A binary semaphore is just a mutex.
issues.problem: Binary semaphores do not enforce ownership; any thread may signal them, whereas mutexes require the owning thread to unlock. Thus they are not interchangeable.
issues.fix: Clarify that a binary semaphore is a special case of a counting semaphore (max = 1) and that it lacks ownership semantics, making it unsuitable as a drop‑in replacement for a mutex.

issues.claim: Binary semaphores cannot be signaled when no thread is waiting, and doing so causes nothing bad to happen.
issues.problem: A binary semaphore can be signaled even if no thread is waiting; its value simply increments to 1, allowing the next wait to succeed immediately. This can mask logic errors but is not inherently harmful.
issues.fix: Explain that signaling an unused binary semaphore is allowed and may hide bugs, but it does not cause a runtime error.

issues.problem: Mutexes can still participate in classic deadlock scenarios (e.g., circular wait on multiple mutexes). Ownership does not eliminate all deadlock possibilities.
issues.fix: Add that while ownership reduces certain mistakes, mutexes can still deadlock if multiple locks are acquired in conflicting orders.
